claim: After learning 三日 as 'Three days' and 二日間 as 'Two days', a learner reads 一日 as 'one day', and the back teaches tsuitachi with no hint that 'one day' is a different reading, so the learner comes away thinking 一日 is always tsuitachi.
evidence: Reading back: '一日 / Answer: The 1st (day of the month) / Says: tsuitachi'. Earlier cards: '三日 | Three days' (chapter-17), '二日間 | Two days' (chapter-16). 一 card gives only 'ichi, it-, itsu / hito'.
fix: Add a note that 一日 read as tsuitachi is the 1st of the month, and that the same characters meaning 'one day' are read ichinichi.
verdictReason: Faithful to the book: Kanji Practice C glosses 一日 only as ついたち, and the deck never teaches いちにち (no card in the ledger has that reading; the book prints 一日 いちにち only in the Lesson 6 title and one Lesson 11 dialogue line, which rule 1 does not card). A reading card carries no note (docs/card-rules-reading.md: no scene, hint or note), so the proposed fix has nowhere to go.

claim: The date cards gloss N日 only as 'The Nth (day of the month)', while the previous unit taught 三日 with the same kind of reading as 'Three days', so a learner who answers 四日 as 'four days' cannot tell from the back whether that was wrong.
evidence: Reading backs: '四日 / The 4th (day of the month) / yokka', '五日 / The 5th (day of the month) / itsuka', '十日 / The 10th (day of the month) / tōka'. Earlier: '三日 | Three days' (chapter-17).
fix: Gloss the 2nd to 10th and 20th as 'The Nth (day of the month); N days', or add a short note saying the same word counts days.
verdictReason: Faithful to the book: Kanji Practice C teaches 二日 to 二十日 as days of the month only, and no chapter of the book glosses 四日, 五日 or the rest as a count of days, so adding that sense is out of bounds. The one real mismatch in the series is 三日 (RW4 "three days", RW5 the 3rd), which is the Reader finding chapter-17/r-482dccb7367c/book-gap/1.

claim: 才 and 天才 both answer 'Genius', so the learner cannot see what 天 adds to the compound, and nothing links 才 to 歳, which was taught with the same reading and the same 'years old' meaning.
evidence: Reading back: '才 / Answer: Genius; years old / Says: sai'. Same unit: '天才 / Answer: Genius / Says: tensai'. Earlier: '歳 | Age; years old' (pronunciation sai, chapter-16).
fix: Change the english of 才 (r-b27790d8cdf7) to "Talent; years old". No note: a reading card has nowhere to show one.
verdictReason: Checked: 才 ships as "Genius; years old" (KANJIDIC2 gloss; its reviewNote says the book has not taught it) and 天才 in the same unit as "Genius". Preflight is silent because reading-distinct-english groups characters and words separately (src/audit/checks/reading.js). Rule 9 wants the character's own meaning, and "Talent; years old" is a sound gloss that ends the overlap. The 歳 link cannot be done: a reading card carries no note. Fix is the gloss change only.

claim: The chapter glosses 〜さま and its kanji spelling 様 ("Mr./Ms."), but neither form has a card anywhere in the collection.
evidence: Book, postcard vocabulary: "〜さま Mr./Ms. (used in letter writing)"; Japanese addresses note: "(8) 様" = "Mr./Ms." (ruby さま). candidates/coverage.json lists 様 and notes that さま and 様 should merge to the kanji form; reading-report.json instead drops the kana さま to the kana pool, and the kana deck (chapter-26) did not choose it. No cards.json in the collection has 様 or さま.
fix: Add a word card 様 (reading さま, "Mr./Ms. (in letters)") to this unit, with a character-gap card for 様 if the pipeline needs one.
verdictReason: Checked every cards.json in the collection: the only さま hits are 神さま (chapter-25) and ごちそうさまでした (chapter-26); 様 appears nowhere. The chapter teaches the word (postcard glossary "〜さま Mr./Ms. (used in letter writing)", the same list the deck carded では、お元気で from) and prints its kanji 様(さま) in the addresses note, so by rule 2 the card is the kanji form 様 in this unit, not a kana-pool word. The pipeline trail agrees: candidates/coverage.json lists 様 as a gap; reading-report.json dropped さま to the kana pool and the kana deck did not pick it. Suffixes are carded in this collection (じん, ねんせい), so 〜さま is in scope.

claim: This chapter teaches 三日 (みっか) as the 3rd of the month, but the only 三日 card, from RW4, answers only "Three days", so the date sense is carded nowhere.
evidence: Book, Kanji Practice C: "3. 三日" matched to "(h) みっか" in the 一日 to 二十日 date series; RW4 kanji table: "三日(みっか) three days". Card chapter-17 r-482dccb7367c: 三日 "Three days". This unit's other dates read "The 2nd (day of the month)", "The 4th (day of the month)" and so on; reading-report.json drops 三日 here as already carded in Chapter 18.
fix: Give r-482dccb7367c both senses, e.g. "The 3rd (day of the month); three days".
verdictReason: Checked: chapter-17 r-482dccb7367c 三日 ships as "Three days" (RW4 日 table: 三日(みっか) three days). RW5 Kanji Practice C pairs 三日 with みっか in the 一日 to 二十日 date series, and the deck carded the other ten dates from that exercise as "The Nth (day of the month)"; chapter-18 reading-report.json dropped 三日 as already carded in RW4. Rule 3: one written form with two meanings is one item carrying both. The 3rd-of-the-month sense is carded nowhere.

claim: The table teaches 今 (いま, now) and 山 (やま, mountain) as words with one reading each, but both ship only as silent character cards from earlier units, while 私 and 川, taught the same way, are voiced word cards.
evidence: Book: "今(いま) now", "山(やま) mountain". Cards: chapter-4 r-d2130d70a08e 今 "Now" (kon, kin / ima, no audio); chapter-5 r-0e248e5603d3 山 "Mountain" (san / yama, no audio). This unit's as-generated.json had 今 as a word (ttsText いま) under the same id, and chapter-12's had 山 as a word (ttsText やま). chapter-18 r-4bbe59fd177f 私 (watashi) and chapter-12 r-0f6a7e280c00 川 (kawa) carry audio.
fix: Make 今 and 山 voiced word cards (いま, やま), as card rule 4 asks for a kanji the book also teaches as a word.
verdictReason: Checked: chapter-4 r-d2130d70a08e 今 "Now" (pronunciation "kon, kin / ima", no ttsText, no audio) and chapter-5 r-0e248e5603d3 山 "Mountain" ("san / yama", no audio) are silent character cards whose reviewNote says their readings came from this chapter. The RW5 table lists 今(いま) now and 山(やま) mountain as words, and card rule 4 (docs/card-rules-reading.md; src/reading/readingSchemes.js) makes such a kanji one card: the word, with reading and audio. 私 (chapter-18 r-4bbe59fd177f) and 川 (chapter-12 r-0f6a7e280c00) got that treatment. chapter-18/as-generated.json has 今 as a word (ttsText いま) and chapter-12/as-generated.json has 山 as a word (ttsText やま), both under the shipping ids, so the dedup against the earlier character cards is what lost them. The fix lands on chapter-4 and chapter-5, same ids. Id renumbered from other/1 to other/2 because the Learner file already uses chapter-18/-/other/1 for a different finding.

claim: The English "Take care." keeps a trailing full stop that 28 of the collection's 30 greeting cards do not have.
evidence: Book: "では、お元気で Take care." Card: では、お元気で "Take care.". Other greetings read like "Good morning" with no stop; the only other one with a stop is chapter-13 お大事に "Get well soon.".
verdictReason: Checked: the book prints a stop on every greeting gloss ("Good morning.", "Good night.", "Excuse me.") and the deck strips it: 30 of the 32 Greetings cards have none. The two outliers are では、お元気で "Take care." (this unit) and chapter-13 お大事に "Get well soon.". Deck-side consistency, not a book matter; polish.
